location_name: Capital District - Royal Inn Common Room
ambient_description: Crackling hearth flames cast dancing shadows on worn wooden tables. The smell of roasted meat and ale fills the air as travelers share tales of the fog.

location_name: Capital District - Royal Inn Private Chamber
ambient_description: A modest chamber with a straw mattress and woolen blankets. A single candle flickers on the nightstand, keeping the encroaching fog at bay.
The fog rolls thick across the rooftops. You can barely see the outline of nearby buildings through the grey mist. Somewhere below, the city breathes.
Smoke and fog mingle beneath low timber beams. Merchants haggle in hushed tones while sellswords eye each corner with suspicion.
Stone walls weep with moisture. Barrels of wine and ale line the walls, but shadows in the corners suggest this cellar hides more than spirits.
Crystal chandeliers struggle against the gloom. Nobles in fine silks dine on silverware while servants glide silently between tables draped in white linen.
Velvet curtains seal this chamber from prying eyes. The fog seems unable to penetrate here, as if the room itself rejects the outside world.
Tobacco smoke mingles with fog seeping through cracked walls. Dice clatter, coins clink, and dangerous men laugh too loudly at poor jokes.
The fog itself seems darker here. Hooded figures conduct business in the shadows. You feel many eyes upon you, though you see none.
Canvas stalls emerge from the fog like ships in harbor. Hawkers cry their wares while customers jostle through the grey mist, clutching purses tight.
Carved oak doors stand beneath a brass merchant's seal. Guards in guild colors watch all who enter with calculating eyes.
Maps of trade routes cover every wall, pins marking safe paths through the fog-wrapped forests. A heavy ledger sits open on a mahogany desk.
Stone archways frame a garden where monks tend herbs immune to fog's touch. Prayer bells chime softly through the mist.
Rows of desks where scribes copy ancient texts by candlelight. The scratch of quills and whisper of turning pages echo in the vaulted chamber.
Stained glass filters what little light penetrates the fog into rainbow streams. Golden relics gleam on marble altars untouched by the grey outside.
The fog rolls thickest here where land meets the southern sea. Foghorns bellow warnings. Shapes of moored ships loom like wooden ghosts.
The stench of fish guts and salt battles the fog's musty odor. Gulls screech overhead, invisible in the grey. Fresh catch glistens on ice.
Rotting timber and rusted chains. The fog pours through broken windows like water. Something moves in the darkness beyond your torch's reach.
Dried herbs hang from rafters. Glass jars line shelves, filled with colored liquids and preserved specimens. The air smells of lavender and something bitter.
Bloodstains that won't wash clean mark the stone table. Surgical tools gleam in a neat row. Bandages stained rust-red pile in the corner.
Incense burns futilely against the smell of sickness. Patients lie on cots, fevered and delirious. Healers move between beds wearing cloth masks soaked in vinegar.
Manicured hedges form a maze in the mist. Rare flowers bloom here, cultivated by gardeners who've learned to work through fog. A fountain trickles softly.
Floor-to-ceiling shelves hold leather-bound volumes. A fire crackles in the marble hearth. The fog cannot reach these precious pages and forbidden knowledge.
Behind a false wall lies the family's true wealth. Gold glints in torchlight. But the dust here is undisturbed—no one has entered in years.
Students in grey robes drift through the fog like spirits themselves, debating philosophy and the nature of the endless mist that imprisons their world.
Tiered wooden benches face a slate board covered in chalk diagrams. A professor lectures on fog patterns and theories of what lies beyond the forests.
Tomes bound in strange leather rest on iron chains. These books speak of the time before the fog, of a world that scholars insist never truly existed.
Smoke from a dozen forges adds to the fog. The ring of hammer on anvil echoes between buildings. Sparks fly like fireflies in the gloom.
The forge burns hot enough to push back the fog. Weapons and tools hang on every wall. The smith's hammer never stops its rhythmic song.
This is where legendary blades are born. The master works alone here, forging weapons said to cut through fog itself. Few are permitted to watch.
Guards peer into the fog-choked forest beyond. Strange sounds echo from between the trees—howls that might be wolves, or might be something worse.
Soldiers huddle around a bonfire, weapons close at hand. No one crosses the forest alone. No one who enters the deep fog ever returns unchanged.
Where forest meets sea, the fog is absolute. The lighthouse beam cuts through it in vain. Somewhere beyond lies the rest of the world—if it still exists.
